title: Acceptance Conditions of the Travel Protection Plans
content:
Acceptance under the Travel Protection Plans is decided before a quotation is produced and again before a
certificate is issued, on three measures the plan itself carries — the declared trip cost, the age of the
oldest insured traveller and the length of the journey — together with the terms on a waiver, on children and on
a journey already begun.

## The rule

1. A plan may only be quoted where the declared trip cost is at or below the plan's ceiling, where the oldest
   insured traveller falls within the plan's age range, and where the journey is no longer than the plan's
   maximum length.
2. A multi-trip plan is quoted on its flat annual premium rather than on the trip cost, and covers its stated
   number of journeys in the policy year, each no longer than the plan's maximum length.
3. A quotation stands for the working day it was produced and is re-rated afterwards, because the rating depends
   on the distance to departure.
4. The pre-existing medical condition waiver is granted only on a plan that offers it, and only where the policy
   is bought within the plan's waiver window counted from the first payment toward the trip. A waiver claimed
   outside that window is refused at issue rather than argued at claim.
5. Children under the plan's free age travelling with an insured adult are covered at no additional premium, and
   are still counted as insured travellers for every per-traveller limit.
6. A traveller already on a journey may not buy cover for it; cover is never issued with retrospective effect.

## The three acceptance tests as a table

| Test | Measured against | Satisfied when |
|---|---|---|
| Declared trip cost | The plan's ceiling on the declared trip cost | The declaration is at or below the ceiling |
| Age | The plan's youngest and oldest accepted traveller | The oldest insured traveller falls within the range |
| Journey length | The plan's longest single journey | The journey is no longer than that |

## Points of judgement

A quotation produced on a Friday stands for that Friday and is re-rated when the traveller returns on the
Monday, whatever was said on the Friday. A child of 9 travelling with an insured parent on a plan whose free age
is 18 adds nothing to the premium, and still counts as one insured traveller when a benefit expressed for each
insured traveller is measured. A traveller who telephones from the airport after departure cannot be covered for
the journey they are on, whatever plan they ask for.
